history.period: 17th century (c.1630 per local tradition; ruins medieval)
history.summary: Haripur (Hariharpur), ~10 miles south-east of Baripada, was the capital of the Bhanja rulers of Mayurbhanj before Baripada was founded (tradition: founded 1400 AD by Maharaja Harihara Bhanja after the headquarters moved from Khiching). The Orissa Review (July 2005) lists Radhamohana, Rasikaraya and Jagannath temples among Haripur's ruins. Per local tradition (nuaodisha.com), Raja Harihara Bhanja built the Jagannath temple here ~1630 in Gaudiya style; when Haripur flourished, the Rath Yatra of Jagannath and Radhamohana was celebrated with great pomp, Vardhanapur serving as the idols' halting place. A Haripur Garh travel account (Rangan Datta, 2026) describes a Jagannath temple with a unique two-domed structure showing Gauda (Bengal) influence and a legend linking it to Gajapati Prataprudradeva of Puri. IDENTITY/LOCATION FLAGS: (1) identity is provisional — documented only through travel accounts and local tradition, no authoritative ASI/gazetteer record found; (2) coordinates are the geocoder's district-level match for Haripur village, approximate — verify on the ground; (3) one source says the temple was demolished and the Jagannath idol taken to Pratapapur, so this may be a ruined/inactive shrine; (4) the representative image shows the Rasika Raya brick temple at Haripur Gada (same complex, official Odisha Tourism photo) — no verified standalone photo of the Haripur Jagannath temple itself was found.
